simplifying_expressions.title: Count the x's, count the numbers
simplifying_expressions.explanation: x-terms and plain numbers never mix — combine each separately.

solving_linear_equations.title: An equation is a balance
solving_linear_equations.explanation: Whatever you do to one side, do to the other. Peel away everything until x stands alone.

factorising_common_factor.title: Factorising undoes multiplying
factorising_common_factor.explanation: Pull out the biggest number that divides every term. Expand your answer back out to check it.

factorising_quadratics.title: Find two numbers that multiply and add
factorising_quadratics.explanation: x² + bx + c factors into (x+p)(x+q) exactly when p×q = c and p+q = b.

solving_quadratic_equations.title: Zero times anything is zero
solving_quadratic_equations.explanation: Once factored, either bracket alone can be the zero one — each gives a solution.

simultaneous_equations.title: Two lines cross at exactly one point
simultaneous_equations.explanation: One equation alone isn't enough info. The second pins down the single (x, y) that satisfies both.
simultaneous_equations.example: x + y = 7 and x - y = 3 → add them: 2x = 10 → x = 5, y = 2.

inequalities.title: A negative flips the direction
inequalities.explanation: Multiplying or dividing by a negative reverses which side is bigger — so the inequality sign flips too.

slope_two_points.title: Slope is just rise over run
slope_two_points.explanation: Walk from one point to the other. Slope is how far you go up, divided by how far you go across.

slope_intercept_form.title: y = mx + c is two facts about a line
slope_intercept_form.explanation: m is the steepness, c is where it crosses the y-axis. Rearranging doesn't change the line — it just makes those two facts easy to read.

equation_given_point_slope.title: A point plus a slope is the whole line
equation_given_point_slope.explanation: Every point on a line obeys y = mx + c. Plug in what you know, solve for the one thing you don't.
equation_given_point_slope.example: Slope 2 through (3, 1): 1 = 2(3) + c → c = -5. Line: y = 2x - 5.

parallel_lines.title: Parallel means same slope, different line
parallel_lines.explanation: Same steepness, different starting point. Copy the slope, work out a new c for the new point.

perpendicular_lines.title: Perpendicular is -1/m, not m × -1
perpendicular_lines.explanation: Rotate a line 90° and rise/run swap AND one sign flips — that's a negative reciprocal, not just a sign change.
perpendicular_lines.example: Slope 2 → rise 2, run 1 → rotate → rise 1, run -2 → slope -1/2, not -2.

midpoint.title: A midpoint is two averages
midpoint.explanation: Average the x's, average the y's, separately. That's the whole method.

distance.title: Distance is Pythagoras in disguise
distance.explanation: The gap between two points is a right-angled triangle's hypotenuse — the horizontal and vertical gaps are the two legs.

axis_intercepts.title: An intercept is where one coordinate is zero
axis_intercepts.explanation: On the x-axis, y is always 0. Set y = 0 and solve for x.
